## 3. The evidence that moved it




**Three negative checkpoint phase 3s in one month.**
[BR.31](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41529222/) finds no disease-free survival benefit for adjuvant
durvalumab in resected NSCLC at any PD-L1 level;
[KEYVIBE-010](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41698381/) finds no recurrence-free survival benefit from adding
anti-TIGIT to pembrolizumab as adjuvant melanoma therapy; and
[LU005](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41529214/) finds no survival benefit from adding atezolizumab to
chemoradiation in limited-stage small-cell lung cancer. All three are the same
design move — take an agent that works in advanced disease and push it earlier or
add it to a backbone — and all three fail. The adjuvant setting is where this
corpus should now expect checkpoint combinations to fail by default.

**A target was killed by a reagent artifact.** [41871876](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41871876/) (*JITC*)
reports that the high BCMA expression reported in AML is an artifact of
nonspecific Fc binding, and that anti-BCMA CAR-T barely lyses AML cells. This is
the most economical refutation in the corpus: one antibody-validation control
removes an entire proposed indication for a platform that already works
elsewhere.

**Agentic AI produced three genuine supports in a single month**, the first time
that has happened: [collective intelligence for AI-assisted chemical
synthesis](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41554982/), an [agentic system for rare-disease diagnosis with
traceable, auditable reasoning](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41708847/), and
[LUMI-lab](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41742414/), a foundation-model-driven autonomous platform that
discovers ionizable lipid chemistry. The auditability of the second is the
notable feature — it is the first agentic paper in the corpus whose selling point
is that its reasoning can be checked rather than that it works.

**Vaccines reached unaffected people.** [41545594](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41545594/) tests the
Nous-209 shared-frameshift-neoantigen vaccine in *unaffected* Lynch syndrome
carriers, and [41818359](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41818359/) (*Science*) reframes KRAS inhibition as
prevention in precursor lesions rather than treatment of advanced disease. Both
sit at the join between `neoantigen-vaccines` and `interception`, and both move
the intervention point earlier than any trial this corpus has previously
recorded.

## 4. Refutations

### (a) Landing on a tracked thread

[41512868](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41512868/) (*Cancer Cell*): IGLL5-positive B cells *disassemble*
tertiary lymphoid structures. TLS have been treated across this corpus as a
favourable feature to induce, and the B cell compartment as what builds them.
Together with the September 2025 finding that Treg- and MDSC-rich TLS mark fatal
cervical cancer, the position now is that TLS presence is not a biomarker and TLS
induction is not obviously a goal — what matters is which cells are in them.

### (b) Method credibility

[40790276](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40790276/) (*Nat Biomed Eng*): latent diffusion models memorize
patient imaging data, so synthetic medical images are not privacy-preserving.
This is filed under method credibility rather than foundation models on purpose —
it is not a capability limit, it is a claim that a stated property of a deployed
technique is false.

[41772176](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41772176/): histology-based molecular biomarker models learn
clinicopathological confounders rather than molecular state. Read against
[41372473](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41372473/) from December — foundation models in oncology win
benchmarks and miss the clinic — this supplies the mechanism for the miss.

[41763219](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41763219/) (*Cell Syst*): CRISPRa activation levels are confounded
by shared cellular resources rather than by guide or target biology. Every
CRISPRa screen that reads activation strength as a biological quantity inherits
this.

[41653917](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41653917/): prior cfDNA end-motif and fragmentomic analyses used
partial end representations, biasing published classifiers. Second consecutive
month with a cfDNA-classifier artifact, after February's demographic-bias card.
